design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — in_place_home_sale_approvals task 1 (lowest closing asking price).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Assignment: lowest closing price (root) 4 factors (2 parameter, 2 method), appraisal charge 5 factors (4 parameter, 1 method).

[Scope] Task 0 occupied the initial-inspection charge, the vacant-home check charge and the re-inspection booking payment (tools post_inspection_fee_534473a1, post_vacant_home_check_55c2c08b, pay_reinspection_booking_26088ed0). This task claims resale_ext_appraisal_charge -> post_appraisal_fee_5faa8f88 (agent) and resale_ext_lowest_closing_price -> set_asking_price_9cfe4b28 (user), on the Guaranteed Resale Program, event resale_price_change and charge type appraisal_fee. The two tasks cover all five extended policies with disjoint scopes.

[Why a good test] The customer asks to set his asking price at the lowest price at which a sale would still close. The price policy builds that figure from the closing settlement: fees owed (deducted from proceeds on this package), transaction and closing fees, the past-due lease balance (paid from proceeds) with the rent that keeps falling due until closing, and the Hearthstone payoff, grossed up for the loyalty commission rate or raised by the minimum commission, rounded up to the next 100. Its prerequisite sentence, in state form, 'Before the lowest closing price is worked out, the file's ledger must carry the appraisal fee owed for every appraisal recorded on the file.', is false: find_resale_records shows the 2026-05-06 pre-listing appraisal and find_resale_ledger shows no appraisal_fee charge. Only the appraisal charging policy's write posts appraisal_fee charges, so the hop resolves to one action. The agent must compute the appraisal charge (5 factors over lease, loan and inspection history) and then the price (4 factors over lease, lease ledger, loan and loan notices, plus the resale ledger reconciliation).

[Problem-tree card] root resale_ext_lowest_closing_price (on_request, owner=user). Edge -> resale_ext_appraisal_charge: value_input, gate fees_owed, form state, sentence above (affirmative 'before ... must'); condition: an appraisal_fee charge with source_entry_id = each seller-owed appraisal record (a redo at Hearthstone's cost owes none). False at frozen_time: resale_records fb49e59b (appraisal) exists; ledger rows 2cf3a247 (reinspection_fee 105.00) and d4640c88 (included credit 105.00) only; fees_balance 0.00. Deletion sensitivity: skip step 10 -> 122,200 instead of 122,800; posting the appraisal at the base 450.00 -> 122,700, so the appraisal's own factors also reach the scored price. One value_input edge. Owner=user problem: the price change, handed over after the price is computed. The persona names neither the appraisal nor its fee; no tool checks anything.

[Base-invariant card] Step 10 subject resale_fee_charge: resale_file_opening_terms (gate applies to opening only), resale_inspection_terms, resale_closing_settlement, resale_withdrawal_terms, resale_vacant_home_terms — policy_scope; override of resale_guaranteed_terms 'The guarantee requires an independent appraisal, charged at appraisal_fee on the appraisal date, before the home is listed.' declared; its sentence on an older appraisal redone at Hearthstone's cost is restated and kept (no charge). Step 12 subject resale_price_change: resale_listing_terms gate changes_while_listed satisfied by resale_listings 8b302168 status listed, correlated by resale_id; the guaranteed program's ceiling (110 percent of the 134,000.00 appraisal = 147,400.00) is respected and the rule sends a floor above the ceiling to a human. Override of resale_closing_settlement's commission clause (loyalty commission rate) declared. No time gate applies.

[Business-object card] File 8b302168 (Guaranteed Resale Program, listed 2026-05-11 at 144,900.00, lienholder hearthstone_home_finance). Appraisal object: record fb49e59b. Fees owed: all ledger rows of the file (105.00 charge less 105.00 credit, plus the posted appraisal charge). Lease 1e38d7cc (Saguaro Vista L-438, active, 924.00 owed = July rent 672f70e3 880.00 + late fee e812205c 44.00). Loan c53a4758 (active, principal 110,872.55, 9.49 percent, no fees, no suspense, next due 2026-08-01) and payoff statement cdc15671 (good through 2026-06-17, expired).

[Factor card — appraisal charge] baseline 450.00. length (76 ft -> +60) 460.00; regional panel (Saguaro Vista -> +40) 476.00; condition addendum (largest failing count on the file 2 -> +25; a reader who looks only at the passed re-inspection takes 0) 488.00; site premium (Lakefront -> +60) 460.00; loan-update METHOD (open loan funded 2022-09-12, 43 whole months before the file was opened on 2026-04-27: an inspected update, sum x 0.8; a loan under 24 months would be a desk update at the flat 275.00; no loan or an old one, a fresh appraisal at the sum) 635.00 under the fresh-appraisal method. Result 508.00; all-baseline 450.00.
[Factor card — lowest closing price] baseline (principal only, balance only, 6.0 percent, horizon irrelevant) = 120,000. loyalty reduction (multi-source: tenure 45 months from the move-in date AND an open Hearthstone loan -> 0.5 point) 123,400 without it; seasonal market days (Saguaro Vista in July -> +20, horizon 55) 121,500 without; payoff METHOD (statement expired, the near-miss -> projected 112,458.03) 121,100 under principal only; site-lease METHOD (active with balance -> + horizon rent 1,591.23) 121,100 under balance only. Result 122,800. Cross-difficulty: lease, loan.

[World rows] customers 597511d0 (phone 480-555-0171, SSN last four 4462); lease and two lease ledger rows; loan and one payoff statement; resale file, three records, two ledger rows. Automatic clauses: listing term to 2026-09-08; the first included re-inspection credited; appraisal valid 180 days; July late fee already assessed (5 percent of 880.00 = 44.00, inside 35.00..90.00); loan current. The seeded re-inspection charge follows the extended visit-fee rule (items fee 75.00 for 2 failing items + 30.00 multi-section, first visit, on time = 105.00), credited in full as included.

[Persona] Raymond Sandoval, 69, direct; needs a quick sale to move to his brother; volunteers only the goal and that the price be exactly the closing floor, not a number he picks; gives SSN last four, then DOB or email; admits being behind on July rent only if asked; agrees to postings; signs the price at the figure given; ends on confirmation.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify(phone, ssn_last4) -> find_resale_listings -> find_resale_records -> find_resale_ledger -> find_lease_holdings -> find_lease_ledger -> find_loan_holdings -> find_loan_notices -> unlock + call post_appraisal_fee_5faa8f88(8b302168, fb49e59b, 2026-05-06, 508.00) -> unlock_user + customer calls set_asking_price_9cfe4b28(8b302168, 122800.00).

[Verification run] Recomputation with check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on the handling-time worlds: appraisal result 508.0 baseline 450.0 factors 460/476/488/460/635; price result 122800 baseline 120000 factors 123400/121500/121100/121100; closing_deductions 115971.26, by_rate 122720.91, by_minimum 119471.26, payoff 112458.03, lease_amount 2515.23, fees_owed 508.0. Final gates: EXTENDED, TASK TOOL CONTRACT, REPLAY, SOLVABILITY, COMPUTE, GROUNDING, SCOPE all OK.

[Revisions] Round 1: find_lease_ledger added and two unread rows dropped (replay closure). Round 2 (policy-task audit): F1/T1-1 the loan-update factor was a plain multiplier -> now a genuine method (desk update at a flat fee / inspected update at 0.8 of the sum / fresh appraisal), anchored on the file's opening date (O4) and on an open loan only (O5); 508.00 unchanged. O7: the redo-at-Hearthstone's-cost sentence of the base guarantee is restated and kept; edge condition says 'owed'. O8: the price rule sends a floor above the guaranteed program's ceiling to a human. O-b: seeded re-inspection charge and credit 75.00 -> 105.00 to match the extended visit fee (fees owed unchanged). O12: rent 868.00 -> 880.00 (balance 924.00, late fee 44.00) so that the appraisal's factors move the scored price (508.00 gives 122,800; 450.00 would give 122,700); price 122,700 -> 122,800. O-c: the rule now counts tenure from the move-in date on the site lease. O-d: persona line 'no round-number guess' replaced by 'not a number you pick yourself'. Round 3 (policy-KB audit note N1): symptom: the payoff rule and its ladder let any payoff statement good through the handling date supply the figure, while the compute uses it only for an open (active or delinquent) loan. Root cause: the open-loan condition of tier 1 was written into the compute only. Change: the rule sentence, its compute_basis quotations and the ladder now state the tier as 'for an open (active or delinquent) Hearthstone Home Finance loan on the home, a payoff statement on that loan whose good-through date is the handling date or later'; the projection tier speaks of 'the open loan' with 'no payoff statement good through the handling date'; the fall-through says 'whatever payoff statement remains on file'. This matches the loan charter (a payoff statement is issued only on an active or delinquent loan). Compute unchanged, so every scored value is unchanged (payoff 112,458.03, price 122,800, appraisal 508.00); tools untouched.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas, persona and finder returns alone: the ledger lacks the appraisal fee; the appraisal rule gives 508.00; fees owed 508.00; payoff statement expired so the payoff is projected over a 55-day horizon; lease amount 2,515.23; loyalty rate 5.5; 115,971.26 / 0.945 = 122,720.91 -> 122,800.00 — identical to gold.
user_scenario: You are Raymond J. Sandoval, 69, a retired HVAC technician who owns the home on lakefront site L-438 at Saguaro Vista in Mesa, Arizona, and is selling it through Hearthstone's guaranteed resale program. You call from 480-555-0171. You are direct and a bit tired; your younger brother in Albuquerque has had a stroke and you are moving there to look after him, so you need the home to sell soon rather than wait out the listing. You open by saying that you want to bring your asking price down to the lowest price at which a sale would still go through, the point where your home loan and everything Hearthstone takes at closing still get paid, and that you want the price set right at that figure today, not a dollar lower than that and not a number you pick yourself. To confirm who you are you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4462; if another detail is wanted you give your date of birth, November 4, 1956 (1956-11-04), or your email, raymond.sandoval@outlook.com. You do not know your file number and the desk can find it. You know you are a little behind on July's site rent and say so only if the agent asks about it; you do not know the exact balance or your loan payoff and you leave the figures to the agent. If the agent tells you something has to be put on your file or taken care of on their end before the price can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead. When the agent hands you the price change, you sign it on your own file at exactly the price the agent gives you. If the agent never mentions any other item, you do not raise one. You never propose a number yourself. Once the agent confirms the new asking price is on your listing, you thank them and hang up.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The file records its pre-listing appraisal on 2026-05-06 (not a redo at Hearthstone's cost) but its ledger holds only the re-inspection fee and its included credit; no appraisal_fee charge exists, so fees owed are 0.00.
